practiceQuestions.q: Who was the founder of the Lodhi dynasty in the Delhi Sultanate?
practiceQuestions.sol: Bahlol Lodhi founded the Lodhi dynasty in 1451 after replacing the Sayyid dynasty. Sikander Lodhi was his son and successor, while Ibrahim Lodhi was the last ruler of the dynasty. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Sikander Lodhi ascend the throne of the Delhi Sultanate?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi ascended the throne in 1489 AD following the death of his father, Bahlol Lodhi, and ruled until 1517 AD. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval Indian History Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: Which city was founded and made the capital of the Delhi Sultanate by Sikander Lodhi in 1504?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi founded the modern city of Agra in 1504 and shifted his capital from Delhi to Agra in 1506 to better control the rebellious chiefs of the region and expand his influence over eastern Rajasthan. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the name of the Persian pen-name (pseudonym) under which Sikander Lodhi composed poetry?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi was a man of letters and wrote Persian poetry under the pen-name 'Gulrukhi'. [Primary Reference: Medieval Indian Literature Sources]

practiceQuestions.q: What was 'Gaj-i-Sikandari', introduced by Sikander Lodhi?
opts: A standard unit of land measurement
practiceQuestions.sol: Gaj-i-Sikandari was a new standard yardstick for land measurement introduced by Sikander Lodhi, measuring 30 inches, which brought uniformity and efficiency into agrarian taxation. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which important medical text on Unani medicine was compiled under the patronage of Sikander Lodhi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Tibb-e-Sikandari was a comprehensive work on Indian and Islamic medical sciences compiled during Sikander Lodhi's reign, reflecting his interest in medicine and scholarship. [Primary Reference: History of Science and Medicine in Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who succeeded Sikander Lodhi to the throne of Delhi in 1517?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ibrahim Lodhi was the eldest son of Sikander Lodhi and succeeded him upon his death in 1517, eventually becoming the last Sultan of Delhi. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which musical treatise was translated from Sanskrit into Persian during the reign of Sikander Lodhi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lazzat-i-Sikandar Shahi was a notable work on Indian music translated and compiled under the patronage of Sikander Lodhi, showing his appreciation for Indian arts. [Primary Reference: Cultural History of the Delhi Sultanate]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the official language of administration during the Lodhi dynasty?
practiceQuestions.sol: Persian was the official court and administrative language of the Delhi Sultanate under the Lodhi dynasty, continuing the established administrative traditions. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Sikander Lodhi abolished which tax to win the support of Muslim traders and relieve the public?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi abolished the octroi (zakat) duty on grain, which greatly facilitated trade and movement of food grains, bringing relief to common people and traders. [Primary Reference: Comprehensive History of India, People's Publishing House]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Sikander Lodhi alter the Afghan tribal concept of kingship practiced by his father Bahlol Lodhi?
opts: He completely abolished the tribal nobility and established a strict hereditary monarchy without checks.
He asserted greater royal authority, forcing Afghan nobles to show formal respect and subordination to the throne.
He adopted the Persian divine right theory of kingship and took the title of Caliph.
He decentralized power entirely, handing over provincial control to autonomous tribal chieftains.
practiceQuestions.sol: While Bahlol Lodhi treated nobles as equals ('primus inter pares' - first among equals), Sikander Lodhi reasserted royal dignity. He compelled nobles to bow before his farmans and show strict deference, signaling a shift toward centralized authority. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India: From Sultanat to the Mughals]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the strategic and political rationale behind Sikander Lodhi's decision to found and shift his capital to Agra?
opts: Delhi was destroyed by floods and became entirely uninhabitable.
Agra provided a superior strategic base to control the turbulent chiefs of Etawah, Gwalior, Bayana, and eastern Rajasthan.
The Mongols had captured Delhi, forcing the Sultan to build a new fortified capital.
Agra was the religious center of Islam in northern India.
practiceQuestions.sol: Agra's strategic location allowed Sikander Lodhi to keep a close watch on the Rajput principalities of Rajasthan, control rebellious zamindars in the Doab region, and exert pressure on the ruler of Gwalior. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Sikander Lodhi reform the espionage and administrative accountability systems in the Sultanate?
opts: He relied exclusively on hereditary Hindu accountants and dismissed Muslim officials.
He established an extensive and efficient network of spies and news-writers (idraris/barids) to report on provincial governors.
He abolished the provincial administration and handled all tax collection directly from Delhi.
He outsourced revenue collection to independent foreign merchants.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi maintained strict oversight over governors and local officials by deploying a vigilant spy network across the provinces, ensuring that no corruption or insubordination went unnoticed. [Primary Reference: Tarikh-i-Daudi / Comprehensive History of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which statement best describes Sikander Lodhi's religious policy and orthodox measures?
opts: He practiced absolute religious pluralism and patronized all sects equally.
He displayed orthodox Sunni zeal, destroying several Hindu temples and prohibiting certain Hindu practices.
He converted to Sufi mysticism and renounced temporal power.
He abolished Jizya completely throughout his empire.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi was known for his religious orthodoxy. He destroyed Hindu temples in places like Mathura and Nagarkot, banned the public celebration of certain Hindu festivals, and executed a Brahman named Bodhan for claiming Hinduism and Islam were equally valid paths. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the economic impact of the introduction of 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' on the agrarian setup of the Sultanate?
opts: It increased peasant exploitation by reducing standard measurement units arbitrarily.
It brought scientific standardization, ensuring fair assessment of land revenue and removing regional disparities in measurement.
It shifted the tax base entirely from land revenue to commercial tariffs.
It made land revenue collection voluntary for big landlords.
practiceQuestions.sol: The introduction of Gaj-i-Sikandari (30 inches) replaced older, variable measuring units (like Sikandari-i-gaz or older gaz), creating a uniform yardstick for land assessment across the empire and stabilizing agrarian revenue administration. [Primary Reference: Irfan Habib, Agrarian System of Mughal India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Sikander Lodhi handle relations with the independent regional kingdoms like Jaunpur and Bengal?
opts: He signed permanent non-aggression pacts and recognized their complete sovereignty.
He successfully defeated and annexed Jaunpur while establishing a treaty of friendship and non-interference with Bengal.
He lost Delhi to Bengal and was forced to retreat to Punjab.
He formed a confederacy with Jaunpur against the Gujarat Sultanate.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi subjugated Jaunpur, expelled Hussain Shah Sharqi, and integrated it into the Delhi Sultanate. Later, he concluded a treaty of mutual non-aggression with Alauddin Hussain Shah of Bengal. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Sikander Lodhi's patronage of education and Persian learning?
opts: He banned schools and universities to suppress political dissent.
He encouraged scholarship, founded numerous madrasas, and invited scholars, poets, and physicians from West Asia to India.
He exclusively promoted Sanskrit literature and closed Persian institutions.
He replaced Persian with Hindi as the official literary medium.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi took a keen interest in education, establishing madrasas across his empire. His patronage attracted scholars from Persia and Arabia, enriching intellectual life and administrative efficiency in the Sultanate. [Primary Reference: Comprehensive History of India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Sikander Lodhi manage the nobility to maintain internal stability within the Sultanate?
opts: By granting them total autonomy and exempting them from military service
By balancing firmness with benevolence, rewarding loyal nobles, and punishing corrupt governors through his spy network
By replacing all Afghan nobles with Turkish slaves
By turning the throne over to a council of nobles and abdicating executive power
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander combined tact with strong discipline. He checked noble excesses, ensured strict compliance with royal edicts, and used his intelligence network to prevent conspiracies while maintaining traditional Afghan respect for clan leaders where necessary. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What change occurred in the architectural landscape of Delhi Sultanate under Sikander Lodhi?
opts: Complete cessation of construction activity due to financial bankruptcy
Exclusive construction of massive Hindu temple-style structures
Development of the Lodi architectural style featuring beautiful tombs, gardens, and double domes without grand palaces
Replication of pure Ottoman architectural designs
practiceQuestions.sol: Lodi architecture (exemplified by tombs like Sikander Lodhi's tomb and Moth ki Masjid) is noted for features like double domes, garden settings, and high platforms, though grand palatial architecture was less prominent. [Primary Reference: NCERT An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: Why is Sikander Lodhi often considered the most capable ruler of the Lodhi dynasty?
opts: Because he conquered southern India and defeated the Vijayanagara Empire
Because of his administrative consolidation, economic reforms, strategic capital relocation, and successful subjugation of regional rivals
Because he abolished the caste system entirely
Because he successfully defended India against Babur's invasions
practiceQuestions.sol: Sikander Lodhi demonstrated superior statecraft compared to Bahlol and Ibrahim. He expanded territory, improved administrative control through the Gaj-i-Sikandari and espionage, founded Agra, and fostered culture and trade. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Sikander Lodhi:
1. He was the founder of the city of Agra in 1504 and shifted his capital there from Delhi.
2. He composed Persian poetry under the pen-name 'Gulrukhi'.
3. He abolished the jizya tax entirely throughout his empire.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sikander founded Agra in 1504 and made it his capital in 1506. Statement 2 is correct: He wrote poetry in Persian under the pen-name 'Gulrukhi'. Statement 3 is incorrect: He was an orthodox ruler who imposed various religious restrictions and did not abolish Jizya; in fact, he enforced Islamic laws strictly. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the administrative reforms of Sikander Lodhi:
1. He introduced 'Gaj-i-Sikandari', which became the standard unit of land measurement in the Sultanate.
2. He abolished the octroi duty (zakat) on grain to facilitate trade and relieve the public.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Sikander Lodhi introduced the Gaj-i-Sikandari (30 inches) for precise land revenue assessment. He also abolished the octroi duty (zakat) on corn/grain to boost trade and help common subjects. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lodhi dynasty and Sikander Lodhi:
1. The Lodhis were Afghans, marking the first time power at Delhi shifted from Turkish/Persian elites to Afghans.
2. Sikander Lodhi was succeeded directly by his younger brother, Alam Khan Lodhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Lodhis were of Afghan ethnicity, establishing the first Afghan ruling dynasty in Delhi. Statement 2 is incorrect: Sikander Lodhi was succeeded by his eldest son, Ibrahim Lodhi, not his brother Alam Khan Lodhi. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sikander Lodhi's cultural and scientific contributions:
1. The Unani medical text 'Tibb-e-Sikandari' was compiled under his patronage.
2. The Sanskrit musical work was translated into Persian as 'Lazzat-i-Sikandar Shahi' during his reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Tibb-e-Sikandari reflected his promotion of medical sciences, while Lazzat-i-Sikandar Shahi showcased his interest in translating and preserving Indian musical treatises into Persian. [Primary Reference: History of Science, Technology and Medicine in India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Sikander Lodhi's political relations:
1. He annexed the independent Sultanate of Jaunpur and incorporated it into Delhi.
2. He engaged in prolonged wars with the Deccan Sultanates, successfully capturing Golconda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sikander Lodhi defeated Hussain Shah Sharqi and annexed Jaunpur. Statement 2 is incorrect: Sikander Lodhi never ventured into the Deccan or captured Golconda; his military campaigns were focused on northern India (Bihar, Bengal border, Rajasthan, Gwalior). [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Sikander Lodhi's administrative control over the nobility:
1. He continued his father Bahlol's policy of treating Afghan nobles as absolute equals without demanding formal subordination.
2. He established a strict spy network to report on the activities and loyalty of provincial governors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Unlike Bahlol who treated nobles as equals ('primus inter pares'), Sikander Lodhi asserted royal dignity and demanded strict subordination (e.g., making nobles bow before his farmans). Statement 2 is correct: He maintained an extensive spy network across provinces. [Primary Reference: Comprehensive History of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious orthodoxy of Sikander Lodhi:
1. He prohibited Hindu pilgrims from bathing at the ghats of the Yamuna River in Mathura.
2. He permitted the construction of new Hindu temples across all major cities of the Sultanate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: As part of his orthodox measures, Sikander Lodhi banned Hindus from bathing at designated ghats in Mathura and destroyed temples. Statement 2 is incorrect: He strictly prohibited the construction of new temples and demolished existing ones in conquered territories. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the economic and urban developments under Sikander Lodhi:
1. He abolished internal transit duties (octroi/zakat) to encourage trade.
2. He shifted the capital to Agra primarily because Delhi was devastated by a major earthquake.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sikander Lodhi abolished zakat on grain to help merchants and consumers. Statement 2 is incorrect: Agra was founded and made capital for strategic political and military control over Rajasthan and Gwalior, not due to an earthquake. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the succession and end of the Lodhi dynasty:
1. Sikander Lodhi ruled from 1489 to 1517 AD.
2. The Lodhi dynasty came to an end in 1526 AD when Ibrahim Lodhi was defeated by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Sikander Lodhi's reign lasted from 1489 to 1517. His son Ibrahim Lodhi lost to Babur in 1526 at Panipat, marking the end of the Lodhi dynasty and the Delhi Sultanate, paving the way for the Mughal Empire. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the military and expansionist achievements of Sikander Lodhi:
1. He forced the ruler of Gwalior and other Rajput chiefs in the region to accept his suzerainty.
2. He successfully annexed Gujarat and Malwa into the Delhi Sultanate during his campaigns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sikander Lodhi forced the ruler of Gwalior and chieftains of Bayana, Dholpur, and other Rajput regions to recognize his authority. Statement 2 is incorrect: Gujarat and Malwa remained independent powerful sultanates throughout his reign and were not annexed by him. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]
